subject: general
question: Which noble gas is radioactive in nature?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Radon**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Radon** is a radioactive noble gas.
 
• It is part of the noble gas group in the periodic table, which also includes helium, neon, argon, krypton, and xenon.
 
• Radon is produced from the natural decay of uranium, which is found in soil, rock, and water.
 
• It is colorless, tasteless, and odorless, making it difficult to detect without specialized equipment.
 
• Exposure to high levels of radon can increase the risk of lung cancer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Radon** was discovered in 1900 by Friedrich Ernst Dorn.
 
• The chemical symbol for radon is **Rn**, and its atomic number is **86**.
 
• Radon levels are typically higher in areas with a lot of granite or other uranium-rich rock formations.
 
• Mitigation systems can be installed to reduce radon levels in buildings.
 
• Radon is used in some types of radiation therapy for cancer treatment.
